top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) turns one conceptual step, the magic wavelength that removes the trap as the limiting systematic, into a many-atom standard whose 10^-18 performance has been reproduced and cross-compared by several independent laboratories. It has concrete consequences for gravitational redshift, constants and dark-matter searches. The citation can name the many-atom lattice clock to separate it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system prizes. The remaining reservations are attribution beyond two names and the overlap with earlier metrology prizes, and neither outweighs the maturity and independent confirmation. P002 (twisted bilayer graphene) is a real prediction-experiment success but younger, with the mechanism unsettled and credit incomplete, and I rely on colleagues in condensed matter; I rank it above no award.
